english.title: Possess / control false document re acting as a gangmaster
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your possession or under your control a relevant document, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DOCUMENT..), that was false and that you knew or believed to be false with the intention of inducing another person to believe that

(A)_[you were]_
(B)_[another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..), acting as a gangmaster in contravention of section 6 of the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004 was]_

acting under the authority of a licence
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(2)(a), (3) and (4) of the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 12(5)(a) provides that for the purposes of this section:- "except in Scotland, a document is false only if it is false within the meaning of Part 1 of the Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981". (see section 9(1) of that Act).

other.penalty:
Summary : maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
